subject: Acme: private connectivity & SDK next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Zhou <sara.zhou@acme-industries.com>, Matt Hooper <matt.hooper@acme-industries.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme: private connectivity & SDK next steps

Hi Sara / Matt,

Thanks again for the call this morning — super helpful to understand Acme's latency and security constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can move to a technical deep-dive with your network team: 

Recap (from our notes)
- Primary requirement: private connectivity for requests to Redwood inference (no public egress from sensitive workloads).
- Desired features: SDK integration for structured-tool-calling + embeddings, ability to pin model versions, and predictable egress IPs for NGFW allowlisting.
- Networking constraints: corporate NGFW in front of egress, DNS forwarding to internal resolvers, and preference for mTLS where possible.

Open technical items we promised to confirm:
1) Supported private deployment patterns (Hosted PrivateLink vs Dedicated vs On‑prem VPC).
2) How auth works inside a private connection (API key vs mTLS + client certs).
3) Egress IP and CIDR ranges we can provide for your allowlist.
4) DNS / split-horizon recommendations for redirecting redwood.ai endpoints to PrivateLink endpoints.
5) Example SDK config for embeddings + reranking (we'll include a minimal YAML).

Attachments I’m including to get started: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (short checklist + ports), sdk-sample-config.yaml (example auth and routing), and a blank network-diagram template so your infra team can drop in topology.

Proposed next steps
- Can you share a contact on your network/security team (name + email)? We’ll set up a 60-minute deep-dive to walk through PrivateLink, DNS, and NAT/egress options.
- If you prefer, we can also schedule an optional 30-minute SDK pairing session to get a dev started with embeddings and structured output.

I’ll list brief answers to the 5 open items in a follow-up message once I confirm with infra, but wanted to get this summary into your inbox.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf), sdk-sample-config.yaml (text/yaml)

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acme: private connectivity & SDK next steps

Thanks, Karthik — nice writeup. A few clarifying Qs before I loop in infra:

1) Which of the private patterns gives us the least infra changes on our side? We prefer to avoid standing up new VPCs if possible.
2) Do you offer static IPs or a small set of egress IPs we can allowlist at the NGFW level? If so, what’s the SLA around those IPs changing?
3) mTLS: is mutual TLS supported for control-plane/auth? We want certificates issued by our internal PKI if possible; otherwise cert rotation becomes a blocker.
4) SDK: can you include a quick code snippet showing how embeddings calls authenticate when using PrivateLink?

Also — we have an internal policy that disallows outbound traffic to public endpoints from our prod subnet. If PrivateLink is available, that sounds attractive.

If you can provide those details, I’ll schedule the network team (likely Dave Chung and Priya Shah) for a technical deep-dive.

—Sara
Platform Engineering Manager
Acme Industries

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Zhou <sara.zhou@acme-industries.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Matt Hooper <matt.hooper@acme-industries.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: private connectivity & SDK next steps

Sara — great questions. Answers below (high-level; we can go deeper on the call):

1) Least-change option: Hosted + PrivateLink (AWS) — requires creating an interface VPC endpoint in your VPC and updating route tables/DNS. No new VPCs required and minimal changes to egress. Dedicated is next — reserved capacity with customer-controlled egress. On‑prem package is available if you need air-gapped install, but that is more involved.

2) Egress IPs: For PrivateLink traffic stays within the AWS fabric so NGFW allowlist is not needed for that path. For scenarios where your services must reach our public API (e.g., Dedicated with customer NAT), we can provide a stable egress IP pool (typically a small set of elastic IPs per region). We publish a weekly change window and provide 30 days notice for changes tied to capacity reconfiguration.

3) mTLS: We support mTLS for Private (customer-managed) deployments and for Dedicated with strict networking. For Hosted PrivateLink endpoints mTLS is supported for the data-plane when you opt-in; control-plane auth uses API keys or OIDC for short-lived tokens. If you need client certs from your internal PKI, our Private/on-prem install allows trusting your CA.

4) SDK snippet (high-level): see sdk-sample-config.yaml attachment — it demonstrates setting endpoint: \"https://private.redwood.internal\" and auth: { method: mTLS / api_key } plus examples for embeddings + reranker. We’ll also paste a runnable Node/Python snippet in the deep-dive.

Additional notes
- DNS: we recommend split-horizon DNS — map api.redwood.ai to the PrivateLink endpoint within your VPC. We can provide the CNAMEs and advise on TTLs.
- Ports: 443 outbound to the interface endpoint for PrivateLink. If you must use NGFW rules, let us know whether you need port-level restrictions; our checklist lists the minimal set.

I’m attaching the checklist and the SDK sample (attached). If that looks good, let’s schedule the 60-minute infra call. I can bring our networking lead (Laura) and our eng PM for Private deployments.

-k

Attachment stubs: sdk-sample-config.yaml (text/yaml), redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
